title: Update: my photo-generated levels went from closet-sized to village-sized, and the puzzles now depend on where a light ends
author: Key-Obligation-1065
selftext:
Two weeks ago I asked here how to design exploration when my photo-generated levels turned out to be the size of a walk-in closet. Thanks to everyone who answered. The idea I keep coming back to is making each room a dense puzzle, so exploring means noticing what doesn't belong instead of walking far.

Quick recap: Unpictured is a gentle first-person puzzle game where each level is generated from a real photo. What the camera saw counts as real. Everything past the frame was invented by a world model, and it's dreamier, with gravity loosening the further you go.

Two updates. First, size: outdoor photos are the opposite problem. A village road came out at about 5,350 m² of walkable floor, 93% of it never seen by the photo, against 3.6 m² in my living room. So I'm keeping dense puzzles everywhere and letting distance do the rest outdoors.

Second, the core mechanic went in this week: memory light. The plan is that each piece of the photo you recover glows, and everything inside its light counts as real again. The rules I'm building toward hang on it:

\- Real light makes you heavy, so the float that got you to the lamp won't get you home while you hold it.

\- Dream bridges and stairs are solid only inside light. Carry a piece to cross one, or plant it to keep the bridge up.

\- A piece's light is as big as the object: a lamp makes a big bubble, a ring a tiny one.

In my test viewer I can now drop up to 8 lights and watch the invented part turn real around each one. I made the edge sharp: the inner 70% of a light is fully real, then there's a short fade. If a bridge stops being solid at the edge of a light, the player has to see exactly where that edge is.

So here's this round's question. Beyond a sharp visual edge, how would you make a light's boundary readable: a ring on the ground, a sound, the bridge flickering as you get close? And should something tiny like a ring still cast a light big enough to be useful?

I'm experimenting and building it with Cline AI. 

Repo: [github.com/MichaelYeh507/Unpictured](http://github.com/MichaelYeh507/Unpictured)
